cards.title: Newborns and Congenital Conditions
cards.content:
The last two lessons were about the **mother's** record. This lesson switches to the **baby's** record and to conditions present from birth.

• **Chapter 16 (P00-P96): Certain Conditions Originating in the Perinatal Period.** For coding purposes, the perinatal period is **before birth through the 28th day following birth**.
• **Chapter 17 (Q00-QA1): Congenital malformations, deformations, chromosomal abnormalities, and genetic disorders.**

You will learn the birth-record principal diagnosis (Z38), when to use Z05 observation codes, which newborn conditions to code, prematurity and low birth weight (P05, P07), newborn sepsis (P36), stillbirth (P95), COVID-19 in newborns, and how to code congenital conditions at any age.

**FY 2027 change:** The chapter 17 title and guideline now include **"genetic disorders"**, and each sentence now says "malformation/deformation, chromosomal abnormality, or genetic disorder."

visual.title: Mother vs Newborn Records
visual.sub: Each chapter stays on its own record

boxes.b: Any age; FY 2027 adds genetic disorders

cards.title: In Plain English: Where Chapter 16 Codes Go (I.C.16.a.1, a.4)
cards.content:
**The record rule (I.C.16.a.1):**

• Chapter 16 codes are **never** used on the **maternal** record.
• Chapter 15 (obstetric) codes are **never** permitted on the **newborn** record.

**The age rule (I.C.16.a.1 and a.4):** Chapter 16 codes may be used **throughout the life of the patient** if the condition is **still present**. If a condition originates in the perinatal period and continues throughout life, keep using the perinatal code **regardless of the patient's age**.

**What it does NOT mean:** The 28-day perinatal period describes when the condition **began**, not a deadline for using the code.

boxes.b: Still use P code if condition present

cards.title: In Plain English: The Birth Record Principal Diagnosis (I.C.16.a.2)
cards.content:
**Birth episode:** Assign a code from **category Z38, Liveborn infants according to place of birth and type of delivery**, as the **principal diagnosis**.

**Only once:** A Z38 code is assigned **only once**, to a newborn **at the time of birth**.

**Transfers:** If the newborn is **transferred** to another institution, the **receiving hospital does not use** a Z38 code.

**Newborn record only:** Z38 is **not** used on the mother's record. (Compare Z37, Outcome of delivery, which goes on the mother's record — Section I.C.15.b.5.)

**Exam trap:** Z37 = mother's record, outcome of delivery. Z38 = baby's birth record, principal diagnosis.

cards.question: A newborn is born at Hospital A and transferred on day 2 to Hospital B for care. According to Section I.C.16.a.2, should Hospital B assign a code from category Z38?
options: Yes, as the principal diagnosis
No, a Z38 code should not be used at the receiving hospital
Yes, as a secondary diagnosis
Only if the newborn is still within the 28-day perinatal period
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.16.a.2 says a Z38 code is assigned only once, to a newborn at the time of birth, and if a newborn is transferred to another institution, a Z38 code should not be used at the receiving hospital. Options A and C are wrong because the receiving hospital does not use Z38 at all. Option D is wrong because the 28-day perinatal period does not change this rule.

cards.title: In Plain English: Other Chapters, Birth vs Community (I.C.16.a.3, a.5)
cards.content:
**Other chapters (I.C.16.a.3):**

• Codes from other chapters may be used with chapter 16 codes if they give **more specific detail**.
• **Sign and symptom** codes may be assigned when a **definitive diagnosis has not been established**.
• If the **reason for the encounter is a perinatal condition**, the chapter 16 code is **sequenced first**.

**Birth process or community acquired (I.C.16.a.5):**

• If a newborn's condition could be **either** due to the birth process **or** community acquired, and the documentation **does not say which**, the **default is the birth process** → use the chapter 16 code.
• If the condition **is documented as community acquired**, do **not** assign a chapter 16 code.
• For COVID-19 in a newborn, the guideline points to Section I.C.16.h.

cards.question: A newborn has a condition that could be due to the birth process or community acquired, and the documentation does not indicate which. Per Section I.C.16.a.5, what should the coder do?
options: Assume it is due to the birth process and use the chapter 16 code
Query the provider and leave the condition uncoded
Assume community acquired and use a code from another chapter
Assign both a chapter 16 code and a community-acquired code
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.16.a.5 says that when the documentation does not indicate which, the default is due to the birth process and the code from chapter 16 should be used. Option B is wrong because the guideline supplies a default for this situation. Option C reverses the default. Option D is wrong because a chapter 16 code is not assigned when the condition is community acquired, so both would not be reported.

cards.title: In Plain English: Code All Clinically Significant Conditions (I.C.16.a.6)
cards.content:
All clinically significant conditions noted on the **routine newborn examination** should be coded. A condition is clinically significant if it requires:

• clinical evaluation; or
• therapeutic treatment; or
• diagnostic procedures; or
• extended length of hospital stay; or
• increased nursing care and/or monitoring; or
• has **implications for future health care needs**

**How this differs from adult rules:** The note says these are the same as the general guidelines for "additional diagnoses," **except** the last point, **implications for future health care needs**. That point is special to the newborn guidelines. Code conditions that the **provider has specified** as having implications for future health care needs.

visual.title: Clinically Significant?
visual.sub: Any ONE of these is enough

cards.question: According to the note in Section I.C.16.a.6, which criterion for a clinically significant newborn condition is NOT part of the general guidelines for additional diagnoses?
options: Requires therapeutic treatment
Requires diagnostic procedures
Requires increased nursing care and/or monitoring
Has implications for future health care needs
cards.explanation: Correct: The note in Section I.C.16.a.6 says the perinatal guidelines are the same as the general coding guidelines for additional diagnoses, except for the final point regarding implications for future health care needs. Options A, B and C are listed in the same section as criteria that match the general additional-diagnosis guidelines.

visual.hint: Look at the final point and the note.

cards.title: In Plain English: Z05 Observation Codes (I.C.16.b)
cards.content:
**What Z05 is for (I.C.16.b.1):** Category **Z05, Observation and evaluation of newborn for suspected diseases and conditions ruled out**, is used when a **healthy newborn** is evaluated for a suspected condition that, **after study, is not present**.

**When NOT to use Z05:** If the newborn has **signs or symptoms** of the suspected problem, **code the sign or symptom** instead.

**Placement:**

• **On the birth record (I.C.16.b.3):** Z05 is a **secondary** code, **after** the Z38 code.
• **On other records (I.C.16.b.2):** Z05 may be the **principal or first-listed** code for readmissions or encounters when the Z38 code no longer applies.

**Who qualifies:** Z05 codes are only for **healthy newborns and infants** for which **no condition is found** after study.

visual.title: Z05: Suspected, Ruled Out
visual.sub: Healthy newborn, nothing found after study

cards.title: Example: Z05 on the Birth Record
cards.content:
**Documentation:** A healthy newborn is born in the hospital. A condition is suspected, the baby is evaluated, and after study the condition is ruled out. The baby has no signs or symptoms of it.

**Guidelines:** Sections I.C.16.a.2 and I.C.16.b.1/b.3.

**Decision:** Z38 code as the **principal** diagnosis, followed by a Z05 code as a **secondary** diagnosis.

**Variation 1:** The baby has a **symptom** of the suspected problem → code the **symptom**, not Z05.

**Variation 2:** The baby is brought back days later for evaluation of a suspected condition that is ruled out → Z05 may be **first-listed**, since Z38 no longer applies.

cards.question: A newborn on the birth admission is evaluated for a suspected condition and shows a related symptom. According to Section I.C.16.b.1, how is this coded?
options: Z38 code, then a Z05 code
Z05 code as principal
Z38 code, then the code for the sign or symptom
Z05 code and the symptom code together
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.16.b.1 says not to use a Z05 code when the patient is documented to have signs or symptoms of a suspected problem; code the sign or symptom. On the birth record, Z38 remains the principal diagnosis (Section I.C.16.a.2). Options A, B and D are wrong because Z05 is not used when signs or symptoms are documented; Option B also ignores that Z38 is principal on the birth record.

visual.hint: Is the baby truly without signs or symptoms?

cards.title: In Plain English: Coding Additional Perinatal Diagnoses (I.C.16.c)
cards.content:
**I.C.16.c.1:** Assign codes for conditions that:

• require **treatment** or **further investigation**,
• **prolong the length of stay**, or
• require **resource utilization**.

**I.C.16.c.2:** Assign codes for conditions that the **provider has specified** as having **implications for future health care needs**.

**Important note:** The guideline says the "future health care needs" rule **should not be used for adult patients**.

**What it does NOT mean:** The coder does not decide on their own that a condition has future implications. The provider must specify it.

boxes.b: Code if provider specifies future implications
This rule should not be used

cards.question: Per Section I.C.16.c.2, which statement about coding conditions with implications for future health care needs is correct?
options: The coder may decide which conditions have future implications
Codes are assigned when the provider has specified the condition has implications for future health care needs, and the rule should not be used for adult patients
The rule applies equally to adult patients
These conditions are coded only if they prolong the length of stay
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.16.c.2 says to assign codes for conditions that the provider has specified as having implications for future health care needs, and its note says this guideline should not be used for adult patients. Option A is wrong because the provider must specify it. Option C contradicts the note. Option D is wrong because prolonging the stay is a separate reason under Section I.C.16.c.1, not a requirement for c.2.

visual.hint: Who specifies it, and for which patients?

cards.title: In Plain English: Prematurity and Birth Weight (I.C.16.d)
cards.content:
**Documentation required:** Providers use **different criteria** to determine prematurity, so a code for prematurity **should not be assigned unless it is documented**.

**Categories involved:**

• **P05**, Disorders of newborn related to slow fetal growth and fetal malnutrition
• **P07**, Disorders of newborn related to short gestation and low birth weight, not elsewhere classified

Codes from these categories are based on the **recorded birth weight** and **estimated gestational age**.

**Two P07 codes:** When **both** birth weight and gestational age are available, assign **two codes from P07**, with **birth weight sequenced before gestational age**.

cards.title: In Plain English: Low Birth Weight Later in Life (I.C.16.e)
cards.content:
**What it says:** P07 codes may be used for a **child or adult** who was **premature or had a low birth weight as a newborn** and this is **affecting the patient's current health status**.

**The condition for using it:** It must be affecting the patient's **current** health status. A history of prematurity alone, with no current effect, does not meet this guideline.

The guideline cross-references Section I.C.21 (Factors influencing health status and contact with health services, Status).

visual.title: P07 Beyond the Newborn
visual.sub: Only if it affects current health

cards.question: A premature newborn's record documents both the birth weight and the estimated gestational age. According to Section I.C.16.d, how is this coded?
options: Two P07 codes, with birth weight sequenced before gestational age
One P07 code for gestational age only
Two P07 codes, with gestational age sequenced first
One P05 code for birth weight and one P07 code for gestational age
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.16.d says that when both birth weight and gestational age are available, two codes from category P07 are assigned, with the code for birth weight sequenced before the code for gestational age. Option B is wrong because both values are coded. Option C reverses the order. Option D is wrong because the guideline calls for two codes from category P07.

cards.question: An adult patient was born with low birth weight, and the provider documents that this is affecting the patient's current health status. Per Section I.C.16.e, can a code from category P07 be used?
options: No, P07 codes are only for newborns
No, only a personal history code may be used
Yes, but only during the 28-day perinatal period
Yes, because the low birth weight is affecting the patient's current health status
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.16.e says P07 codes are for use for a child or adult who was premature or had a low birth weight as a newborn and this is affecting the patient's current health status. Options A and C are wrong because the guideline extends P07 to children and adults. Option B is wrong because the guideline directs P07 when the current health status is affected.

cards.title: In Plain English: Bacterial Sepsis of Newborn (I.C.16.f)
cards.content:
**Category P36, Bacterial sepsis of newborn**, includes **congenital sepsis**.

**Default:** If a perinate is documented with sepsis **without** documentation of congenital or community acquired, the **default is congenital** → assign a **P36** code.

**Organism codes:**

• If the P36 code **includes** the causal organism → do **not** add a code from **B95** or **B96**.
• If the P36 code **does not include** the organism → **add a code from B96**.

**Severe sepsis:** If applicable, add codes for **severe sepsis (R65.2-)** and any associated **acute organ dysfunction**.

**Exam trap:** Compare puerperal sepsis O85 (mother), which always needs an organism code (Section I.C.15.k). For P36, the organism code depends on whether the P36 code already names it.

visual.title: P36 Organism Rule
visual.sub: Does the P36 code name the organism?

cards.question: A perinate is documented with sepsis, with no documentation of whether it is congenital or community acquired. The P36 code assigned does not include the causal organism. According to Section I.C.16.f, what is correct?
options: Assign a code from category A41 only
Assign a P36 code only; organism codes are never added
Assign a P36 code and an additional code from category B96
Assume community acquired and do not use P36
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.16.f says that without documentation of congenital or community acquired, the default is congenital and a P36 code is assigned; if the P36 code does not include the causal organism, an additional code from category B96 is assigned. Option A is wrong because the guideline directs P36 for this newborn. Option B is wrong because B96 is required when the P36 code lacks the organism. Option D reverses the default.

visual.hint: Default source, then check for the organism.

cards.title: In Plain English: Stillbirth, Code P95 (I.C.16.g)
cards.content:
**Code P95, Stillbirth**, has three firm limits:

• It is **only** for use in institutions that **maintain separate records for stillbirths**.
• **No other code** should be used with P95.
• P95 should **not** be used on the **mother's** record.

boxes.b: Only facilities with separate stillbirth records

cards.question: Which statement about code P95, Stillbirth, is correct according to Section I.C.16.g?
options: It is assigned on the mother's record after a stillbirth
It is used only in institutions that maintain separate records for stillbirths, and no other code is used with it
It is sequenced after a code from category Z38
It is used with manifestation codes to describe the cause
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.16.g says P95 is only for use in institutions that maintain separate records for stillbirths, no other code should be used with P95, and it should not be used on the mother's record. Option A contradicts the last rule. Options C and D are wrong because no other code should be used with P95.

cards.title: In Plain English: COVID-19 in a Newborn (I.C.16.h)
cards.content:
**Newborn tests positive, no documentation of how it was transmitted:** Assign **U07.1, COVID-19**, plus codes for associated manifestation(s) in neonates/newborns.

**Provider documents it was contracted in utero or during the birth process:** Assign **P35.8, Other congenital viral diseases**, and **U07.1, COVID-19**.

**Birth episode:** On the newborn's birth record, the appropriate **Z38** code is still the **principal diagnosis**.

**What it does NOT mean:** The birth-process default from Section I.C.16.a.5 does not decide this; the guideline here says to use U07.1 (without P35.8) in the absence of documentation indicating a specific type of transmission.

cards.question: A newborn on the birth admission tests positive for COVID-19. The provider documents that it was contracted during the birth process. According to Section I.C.16.h, which codes apply?
options: Z38 code as principal, plus P35.8 and U07.1
U07.1 as principal, then a Z38 code
Z38 code as principal, plus U07.1 only
P35.8 as principal, then U07.1
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.16.h says that when the provider documents the COVID-19 was contracted in utero or during the birth process, assign P35.8 and U07.1, and on the birth episode the Z38 code is the principal diagnosis. Option B is wrong because Z38 is principal on the birth record. Option C is wrong because P35.8 is required when transmission in utero or during birth is documented. Option D is wrong because Z38, not P35.8, is principal on the birth episode.

visual.hint: Transmission was documented; it is the birth stay.

cards.title: In Plain English: Coding Congenital Conditions (I.C.17, part 1)
cards.content:
**When to code:** Assign code(s) from **Q00-QA1** when a **malformation/deformation, chromosomal abnormality, or genetic disorder** is documented.

**Position:** It may be the **principal/first-listed** diagnosis **or** a **secondary** diagnosis.

**Manifestations:**

• If the condition **does not have a unique code**, assign additional code(s) for any **manifestations** present.
• If the code **specifically identifies** the condition, **do not separately code** manifestations that are an **inherent component** of the anomaly.
• **Do** assign additional codes for manifestations that are **not** an inherent component.

cards.title: In Plain English: Congenital Conditions Over a Lifetime (I.C.17, part 2)
cards.content:
**Any age:** Chapter 17 codes may be used **throughout the life of the patient**.

**Diagnosed later:** A condition present at birth may not be identified until **later in life**. Whenever the provider diagnoses it, it is appropriate to assign a code from **Q00-QA1**.

**Corrected:** If a congenital malformation or deformity has been **corrected**, use a **personal history code** to identify the history.

**Birth admission:** The **Z38** code is sequenced as the **principal** diagnosis, **followed by** any congenital anomaly codes from **Q00-QA1**.

**FY 2027 change:** The chapter title and guideline now name **genetic disorders** along with malformations, deformations, and chromosomal abnormalities.

cards.question: An adult is diagnosed by the provider with a congenital malformation that was present at birth but never identified before. According to Section I.C.17, what is appropriate?
options: A personal history code, because the condition began at birth
A code from chapter 16, because the condition originated in the perinatal period
No code, because chapter 17 codes are limited to the birth admission
A code from Q00-QA1, because chapter 17 codes may be assigned whenever the provider diagnoses the condition
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.17 says a condition present at birth may not be identified until later in life, and whenever it is diagnosed by the provider, it is appropriate to assign a code from Q00-QA1; chapter 17 codes may be used throughout the life of the patient. Option A is wrong because a personal history code is for a malformation or deformity that has been corrected. Option B is wrong because the guideline directs Q00-QA1 for these conditions. Option C contradicts the lifetime rule.

cards.question: A congenital condition has a specific code that identifies it. One manifestation is an inherent component of the anomaly, and another manifestation is not. Per Section I.C.17, what is coded?
options: The chapter 17 code only
The chapter 17 code plus both manifestations
The chapter 17 code plus only the manifestation that is not an inherent component
Only the two manifestation codes
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.17 says that when the code specifically identifies the condition, manifestations that are an inherent component should not be coded separately, and additional codes should be assigned for manifestations that are not an inherent component. Option A misses the non-inherent manifestation. Option B wrongly codes the inherent one. Option D omits the chapter 17 code, which is assigned when the condition is documented.

cards.title: Applying the Newborn and Congenital Rules
cards.content:
1. **Confirm the record:** baby's record → chapter 16 and Z38 codes are allowed, chapter 15 codes are not (I.C.16.a.1–a.2).
2. **Birth episode?** Z38 is principal; only once; not at a receiving hospital after transfer (I.C.16.a.2).
3. **Suspected condition ruled out?** Z05 after Z38 on the birth record, or first-listed on a later encounter; if signs/symptoms exist, code them instead (I.C.16.b).
4. **Which conditions to code?** Clinically significant ones (evaluation, treatment, diagnostics, longer stay, more nursing care, or provider-specified future health care needs) (I.C.16.a.6, I.C.16.c).
5. **Unclear source?** Default to birth process / congenital (I.C.16.a.5, I.C.16.f), except COVID-19 (I.C.16.h).
6. **Prematurity / birth weight:** only if documented; two P07 codes, weight before age (I.C.16.d).
7. **Sepsis:** P36; add B96 only if the P36 code lacks the organism (I.C.16.f).
8. **Stillbirth:** P95 alone, only where separate stillbirth records exist (I.C.16.g).
9. **Congenital condition:** Q00-QA1 at any age; manifestations only if not inherent; personal history code if corrected; Z38 before Q codes on the birth admission (I.C.17).

visual.title: Newborn Record Checklist
visual.sub: Work through the record in this order

boxes.b: Default source; P07 weight then age

cards.title: Key Takeaways
cards.content:
• **Perinatal period** = before birth through day 28. Chapter 16 codes never go on the mother's record; chapter 15 codes never go on the newborn's. P codes continue for life if the condition is present (I.C.16, I.C.16.a).
• **Z38** is the birth-record principal diagnosis, assigned once, not at a receiving hospital (I.C.16.a.2).
• **Default** for birth-process vs community acquired: birth process (I.C.16.a.5); sepsis default: congenital, P36 (I.C.16.f).
• **Z05**: healthy newborn, condition ruled out; never when signs/symptoms are present; secondary after Z38 on the birth record (I.C.16.b).
• **Future health care needs** is a newborn-only reason to code, and the provider must specify it (I.C.16.a.6, I.C.16.c).
• **P07**: weight before gestational age; prematurity only if documented; P07 later in life only if affecting current health (I.C.16.d–e).
• **P95** stands alone. **COVID-19** newborn: U07.1; add P35.8 if in utero/birth transmission is documented (I.C.16.g–h).
• **Chapter 17 (FY 2027 now includes genetic disorders):** Q00-QA1 at any age; skip inherent manifestations; history code once corrected; Z38 first at birth (I.C.17).

cards.question: According to Section I.C.16, how is the perinatal period defined for coding and reporting purposes?
options: From conception through delivery
Before birth through the 28th day following birth
From the last month of pregnancy to five months after birth
From birth through six weeks after birth
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.16 defines the perinatal period as before birth through the 28th day following birth. Option C is the peripartum period from Section I.C.15.o.1, and Option D resembles the six-week postpartum period from the same section; both describe the mother, not the perinatal period. Option A is not a definition in the guidelines.

cards.question: On a newborn's birth admission, the provider documents a congenital anomaly. Per Section I.C.17, how is the record sequenced?
options: The Z38 code first, followed by the congenital anomaly code(s) from Q00-QA1
The congenital anomaly code first, then the Z38 code
A code from category Z37 first, then the anomaly code
Only the Z38 code; anomalies are coded at a later encounter
cards.explanation: Correct: Section I.C.17 says that for the birth admission, the appropriate Z38 code is sequenced as the principal diagnosis, followed by any congenital anomaly codes in Q00-QA1. Option B reverses the order. Option C is wrong because Z37 goes on the mother's record (Section I.C.15.b.5), and Z38 is used only on the newborn record. Option D is wrong because the anomaly is coded when documented.

visual.hint: What is always principal on a birth record?
